title: Implement SCIM deprovision dead-letter queue and reconciliation worker
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We see intermittent and unrecoverable failures from some SCIM providers (rate limits, partial 2xx with missing members, inconsistent deletes) that lead to : orphaned user/headless accounts, inaccurate group membership, and missing audit linkage between provisioning attempts and later manual remediation. Existing retry logic and tombstones reduce immediate breakage but do not provide a durable way to surface hard failures for operations and to reconcile drift across systems.

Goal: Add a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for terminal SCIM deprovision events and a reconciliation worker that replays DLQ entries with richer context and human-review hooks. The system should preserve per-org semantics, maintain strong idempotency, attach full event audit traces, and expose manual remediation UI + runbook links. Roll out behind a feature flag and stage to a small set of orgs first.

High-level approach:
- When deprovision requests exhaust retry budget or hit a terminal error class, emit a DLQ message containing the SCIM externalId, attempted op, provider response body, request metadata (headers, etag) and a stable attempt-id.
- Persist DLQ entries in the event-store with event-sourced audit correlation IDs so they are queryable from the console and audit logs.
- Reconciliation worker pulls DLQ entries (lease-locked per-org) and attempts targeted remediations using enriched strategies: group-membership delta reconciliation, conditional undelete + suspend-then-delete, and back-channel re-sync with the IdP (when supported).
- Provide an operator UI to triage DLQ items with playbook actions: retry-from-DLQ, mark-manual-resolution, escalate-to-support, or schedule-deferred deletion. All actions create an audit trail linked to the original provisioning event.
- Maintain idempotency by using externalId + attempt-id + operation-hash. Use ETag/If-Match where provider supports it to detect concurrent changes and avoid blind deletes.
- Emit metrics/alerts: DLQ-size-by-org, DLQ-ingest-rate, reconcile-success-rate, reconcile-latency, and time-to-manual-resolution. Add SLOs for median reconcile time for P0 orgs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not rework the core SCIM client or add new protocol features to providers. It is an operational layer that improves visibility and remediation for terminal errors.
acceptance_criteria: Dead-letter queue storage created and documented; DLQ items contain externals (externalId, org_id), provider response, request headers, etag (if available), and stable attempt-id

Reconciliation worker implemented with lease-based locking (per-org) and feature-flag gating; worker can process DLQ items and execute at least two remediation strategies (retry and group-delta apply)
Operator console view shows DLQ items with links to original audit event, a timeline of attempts, and actions: retry, mark-resolved, escalate, schedule-delete
Idempotency enforced for reconciliation attempts using externalId + attempt-id; duplicate processing does not cause double-deletes or duplicate user creation
Metrics and alerts for DLQ size and reconcile success rate are in place; dashboard added to Console->Security->SCIM provisioning
Runbook and playbook checked into Confluence with escalation steps and sample queries for manual remediation
E2E tests that simulate a terminal 429/5xx from a SCIM provider and confirm DLQ entry creation and successful reconcile retry path
tasks: Add DLQ table to event-store schema and migration script
Augment SCIM client to emit DLQ entries on terminal failures (classify terminal errors)
Build reconciliation worker with per-org lease locking and strategy plugins
Create console UI for DLQ triage and action invocation
Instrument metrics, create Grafana dashboard and PagerDuty alert
Write E2E integration tests and unit tests for idempotency logic
Draft runbook and update support playbooks
migration_plan: Run DB migration in a canary region first and enable DLQ writes behind feature flag. Reconcile-processor will initially be disabled. Enable reconcile worker for two low-traffic sandbox orgs for 48h, validate metrics and audit linkage, then broaden to ~5 beta orgs. After 2 weeks bump to P0 rollout for enterprise orgs. Provide support team with a manual remediation script and link to the new console view. Backfill previously tombstoned records by running a one-time exporter that converts tombstone rows into DLQ entries for manual triage.
comments: 2025-01-10: Spike completed; prototype DLQ schema and sample DLQ message created (see GH PR #5123)
2025-01-17: Security reviewed the draft and requested ETag usage where available to reduce unsafe deletes
2025-01-22: Design (Jordan Brooks) suggested adding 'suspend then delete' as a safer default for enterprise orgs; accepted
2025-01-29: Ops requested per-org backoff caps to avoid reconcile storms during IdP outages
2025-02-03: Canary enabled for orgs: redwood-sandbox-1 and redwood-sandbox-2; initial DLQ items observed and successfully retried for 3 of 5 failures
notes: Leverage existing event-store retention policies; DLQ entries older than 90 days should be archived and summarized
Consider later follow-up to add automated back-channel re-sync with Okta/OneLogin where their APIs support bulk membership queries
Match DLQ audit ID to general audit log ID so security can run end-to-end investigations without manual correlation
